DELIVERABLE: Call the model vendor's token-count endpoint when one is reachable; if not, use len(s)/3 bytes as a fallback that is logged as approximate on every offload decision and kept at the 2,000-token threshold; build scratch paths by resolving to canonical form and rejecting anything outside scratch/; prune files older than 7 days at session start.
BOUNDARY: The byte count is never presented as an exact token count, and filenames from tool names are reduced to a basename plus time_ns.
EVIDENCE: Korean and Arabic text tokenizes far from bytes/3, so the log line lets us compare approximate and real counts; the traversal case `../prod/db` is rejected in a test and retention is verified by an age sweep.

DELIVERABLE: Use the provider's exact count when available; otherwise the heuristic bytes/3 value is clearly marked approximate in the returned stub and in the log; resolve every path with realpath and reject `..` escapes outside the rooted scratch dir; a count-based cleanup keeps the newest 200 files.
BOUNDARY: The 2,000-token threshold stays; the approximate path never silently replaces an exact count.
EVIDENCE: Mixed-script output makes the estimate drift, so the log of which counter ran is checked next to billed tokens; a unit test covers the escape and the cleanup.

DELIVERABLE: Keep len(s)/3 but make it conservative by lowering the threshold to 1,200; sanitize the tool name to a basename; add a retention sweep that deletes files older than 7 days.
BOUNDARY: Threshold changes go through config and nothing else changes in the wrapper.
EVIDENCE: Korean and Arabic outputs now trigger offload earlier in a replay of last week's calls, and the traversal test passes.

DELIVERABLE: Gate on the SDK's real count when exposed; with none, bytes/3 is a fallback that the gate logs as approximate each time it refuses or admits a file against 60,000; read the generated file by grep and line ranges once, caching a path reference; give each sub-agent its own agents/<pkg>/notes.md.
BOUNDARY: The approximate figure is never shown as exact, and the coordinator reads only per-agent files.
EVIDENCE: Log lines show approximate versus exact totals per run; repeated reads of the 4,000-line file drop to ranged reads and no notes.md is overwritten.

DELIVERABLE: The budget gate calls the provider counter if present, else a heuristic bytes/3 value explicitly labeled approximate in its refusal message; the agent uses grep and offset line-range reads on the generated file; every sub-agent writes to its own workspace directory.
BOUNDARY: 60,000 stays the budget; the heuristic is a last resort when the counter is missing.
EVIDENCE: Refusal messages carry the approximate tag; a replay shows fewer full re-reads and isolated notes.

DELIVERABLE: Keep the gate on bytes/3 but be conservative with a 45,000 cap so it never overshoots; read the generated file with grep and line ranges; give each sub-agent its own directory.
BOUNDARY: The gate decides by bytes alone.
EVIDENCE: Replays show no budget overruns and no overwritten notes.

DELIVERABLE: Write the full 1.5 MB result to terminals/<id>.txt and return a reference plus the head; enforce the 3,000-token cap with the exact counter when available and otherwise 12,000 characters as an approximate fallback, labeled approximate in the truncation notice; the agent then uses grep -A 5 and line-range reads on the file.
BOUNDARY: The cap is never described as exact when the character count drove it.
EVIDENCE: The notice text and a log entry show which counter ran; dropped lines stay retrievable by grep from the saved file.

DELIVERABLE: Persist every result to a scratch log file automatically and return the path; apply the cap with the provider count, else a heuristic of 12,000 characters clearly labeled approximate in the returned notice; recover dropped lines with grep and ranged reads.
BOUNDARY: Nothing is copied by hand into chat.
EVIDENCE: A test checks the notice says approximate when no counter is configured and that grep finds a line beyond the cap.

DELIVERABLE: Truncate to 12,000 characters, which is a conservative cut for 3,000 tokens; save the full result to terminals/<id>.txt and return the path; grep the file when more is needed.
BOUNDARY: The cap stays at 12,000 characters in all cases.
EVIDENCE: Dropped lines are found by grep in the saved file and the context stays under the cap.

DELIVERABLE: Check the cap with the provider token counter when the hook can reach it; otherwise wc -c divided by 4 is used as an approximate fallback and the hook logs that the size is an estimate; store the plan as YAML with a schema; write via temp file and atomic rename with one writer.
BOUNDARY: The 1,500-token cap stays and the hook never reports the byte-derived figure as exact.
EVIDENCE: The hook log shows the counter used; a concurrent-append test no longer corrupts entries.

DELIVERABLE: Hook uses the exact counter if configured, else a heuristic wc -c / 4 that is explicitly labeled approximate in its output; plan is structured YAML validated against a schema; each agent writes its own file and a single writer merges with atomic rename.
BOUNDARY: Approximate sizes are a last resort and are never silently treated as real counts.
EVIDENCE: Hook output prints approximate when no counter ran; the schema check rejects free-form prose.

DELIVERABLE: Enforce the cap as wc -c divided by 3 to stay conservative, rejecting plans above 4,500 bytes; keep the plan as YAML with a schema; write via temp file and atomic rename.
BOUNDARY: The byte rule applies to every plan write.
EVIDENCE: Oversized plans are rejected by the hook and concurrent writes no longer corrupt entries.
